facts.statement: Paraplacodus lived during the Middle Triassic period.
Fossils of Paraplacodus were found in Northern Italy and the species was named by Bernhard Peyer in 1931.
facts.quote: The fossils were uncovered in Northern Italy and the species was named in 1931 by Bernhard Peyer.

facts.statement: The name Paraplacodus means "Almost Placodus" because the animal resembles Placodus.
facts.quote: Paraplacodus means "Almost Placodus", in reference to its similarity to Placodus.

facts.statement: Paraplacodus belonged to the unarmored placodontoid group, which resembled a large, scaly, tooth-filled newt.
facts.quote: Most known placodont species can be divided into two groups - the unarmored placodontoids, which would resemble a large, scaly, tooth-filled newt, or the armored cyamodontids, which would resemble a heavily armored turtle; Paraplacodus belonged to the former family.

facts.statement: Paraplacodus was a small reptile measuring about 1.5 meters in total body length.
facts.quote: It was a small reptile, measuring about 1.5 m in total body length.

facts.statement: Specialized anterior teeth suggest that Paraplacodus fed on small, raspberry-shaped macroalgae.
facts.quote: Its specialised anterior teeth suggest that it would have fed on small, raspberry-shaped macroalgae.

facts.statement: Paraplacodus broilii is an extinct placodont sauropterygian that lived from the Anisian to the Ladinian stages of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Paraplacodus broilii is an extinct placodont sauropterygian from the Middle Triassic epoch, from the Anisian until Ladinian stages.

facts.statement: Paraplacodus is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, superorder Sauropterygia, order Placodontia, family Paraplacodontidae, and genus Paraplacodus.
